rv.q: This is hot blooded full bodied entertainment.
Savage’s and Urena’s choreography is a primary reason to see this ZORRO.

Music Theater Works, Zorro, The Musical, boast extraordinary aerial acrobatics, spectacular sword-fighting, and incredible magic. But unfortunately, this musical was more about gypsies, dancing, and a Zorro that never matched the seductive, captivating, and suave Zorro from the original movies.

The real strength and highlight of this production is its music, beautifully sung and danced with fire and forcefulness by an excellent cast, as well as some vibrant swordplay and fight choreography, created by Nick Sandys.
The entire endeavor clocks in at two hours and 45 minutes, including one 15-minute intermission and too many laborious scene changes to count.
The choreography (Laura Savage) is divine with some wonderful numbers by the women and in particular the three female Flamenco dancers (Lina Bulovaite, Jocelyn Leving and Karla Tennies Kozlura).

cn.t: Music Theater Works' production shows ambition with its LatinX representation and Gipsy Kings score, but critics find the musical itself uneven, delivering spirited performances in a familiar tale that doesn't fully distinguish itself.
